accelerator.title: Target Operating Model (TOM) Agent
accelerator.subtitle: AI-accelerated business-process operating model design
accelerator.value_statement: We leverage AI to accelerate target operating model design. The TOM Agent transforms your current-state process and change-impact data into a future operating model — mapping each function's lifecycle, redefining roles, data, and governance, and producing ready-to-run Future Ways of Working that move transformation to the front line faster.

capabilities.rest: current-state & change-impact data (transcripts, CIA, fit-gaps) into a structured operating-model baseline
each function's lifecycle and the value streams across them — where the new system changes inputs, roles, timing & decisions
the model across eight TOM dimensions — from meetings, roles & data through to guest & service outcomes and locations & sourcing
functional areas by people-impact density & severity, testing each design for coherence across the dimensions
the new roles & seats, the value-at-risk from open gaps, and AI role-shifts — from producing analysis to approving recommendations
the benefits register (baseline source & owner per KPI), Future Ways of Working & governance — reconciled to canonical data

functional_groups.lifecycle: Plan > Buy > Allocate > Price/Promote > Replenish > Learn
Forecast > Allocation > Warehouse ops > Store replenishment
Vendor > RFQ > PO > Receipt > Invoice match > Payment

tom_dimensions.current_state: Multiple prep meetings to assemble data from several systems.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: Which meetings can be shortened or eliminated? What new forums (e.g., S&OP) are needed?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Category roles still running legacy processes; data ownership unclear.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: Who owns data at each stage gate? What new seats does the model imply?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Data stitched together manually across systems.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: What reports become self-service? What data-quality gates are needed?
How do shared items and cross-BU handoffs work in one system?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Teams skilled in manual execution and spreadsheet workarounds.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: Where must the team upskill from execution to system governance? As AI handles routine triage, which roles shift from producing analysis to approving recommendations?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Governance drafted; sponsor roles defined but not activated.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: How does the change network operate post go-live? What guardrails govern AI-generated recommendations?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Service-level effects (availability, experience) managed locally, not tracked as outcomes.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: Which service-level outcomes does the model improve, and how are they measured?

tom_dimensions.current_state: Sites run different calendars/costing; sourcing fragmented.
tom_dimensions.future_state_questions: What stays local vs shared? Who owns the single procurement model and vendor master?

roles_and_seats.name: Shared-data steward
roles_and_seats.why: Owns master data quality across BUs in the single system.

roles_and_seats.name: Item-hierarchy council chair
roles_and_seats.why: Arbitrates cross-BU item and hierarchy conflicts.

value_at_risk.why: Net-new capability with no current process; densest cluster of assumed gaps.
Cost method must be agreed before go-live or cost data is unreliable.

vro_tiers.focus: IRR / ROI tracking against the approved business case
Process-level KPIs (forecast accuracy, inventory turns, landed cost)
System usage, training completion, workaround rates, user confidence
Are teams working differently? New meetings held, old workarounds retired
